hong_kong_island.name: 香港島 Hong Kong Island
hong_kong_island.description: The historic and commercial heart of Hong Kong, home to the iconic skyline, colonial heritage, vibrant nightlife, and world-class shopping districts.

areas.name: 中環 Central
areas.description: The central business district — a blend of towering skyscrapers, historic landmarks, luxury shopping, and trendy nightlife.

spots.name: 太平山頂 Victoria Peak
spots.description: The highest point on Hong Kong Island, offering breathtaking panoramic views of the skyline, Victoria Harbour, and the outlying islands. Take the historic Peak Tram (since 1888) for the steepest funicular railway experience. The Peak Tower and Peak Galleria house dining, shopping, and the Sky Terrace 428 observation deck.
spots.location: Victoria Gap, The Peak
spots.tips: Visit at sunset for golden hour + night views. The Peak Tram can have 30-60min queues — book tickets online. Alternatively hike up via the Morning Trail or Lugard Road for free.

spots.name: 中環至半山自動扶梯 Central-Mid-Levels Escalator
spots.description: The world's longest outdoor covered escalator system (over 800m). Connects Central to the Mid-Levels residential area, cutting through SoHo and passing trendy bars, restaurants, antique shops, and street art. Direction changes — down in morning peak hours, up from 10am.
spots.location: Starts at Central Market, runs through SoHo to Conduit Road
spots.tips: Best visited after 10am when going up. Hop on/off at different points to explore side streets. Great for people-watching and discovering hidden bars.

spots.name: 蘭桂坊 Lan Kwai Fong
spots.description: Hong Kong's most famous nightlife district — a small L-shaped alley packed with over 90 bars, clubs, and restaurants. Comes alive after 9pm with expats, tourists, and young locals. Hosts massive street parties on Halloween, New Year's Eve, and St. Patrick's Day.
spots.location: Between D'Aguilar Street and Wyndham Street, Central
spots.tips: Happy hour 5-8pm for cheaper drinks. Weekends get extremely crowded. Try the side streets (Wo On Lane, Wing Wah Lane) for quieter pub vibes.

spots.name: PMQ元創方
spots.description: A creative hub housed in the former Hollywood Road Police Married Quarters (1951). Three floors of designer studios, art galleries, concept stores, cafes, and workshops. The building itself is a Grade III historic building with a charming courtyard.
spots.location: 35 Aberdeen Street, Central
spots.tips: Free entry. Check the calendar for rotating exhibitions and weekend markets. The rooftop has a nice garden and views.

spots.name: 文武廟 Man Mo Temple
spots.description: One of Hong Kong's oldest and most important temples (built 1847). Dedicated to Man Cheong (god of literature) and Mo Tai (god of war). Famous for the giant spiral incense coils hanging from the ceiling — some burn for weeks. Intricate carvings, gilded altars, and a peaceful atmosphere amid the urban bustle.
spots.location: 124-126 Hollywood Road, Sheung Wan
spots.tips: Free entry. Photography allowed. Combine with a walk down Hollywood Road for antique shops. Visit in the morning for fewer crowds.

spots.name: 大館 Tai Kwun
spots.description: A magnificent revitalization of the former Central Police Station compound (built 1864). Three declared monuments — the Police Station, Magistracy, and Victoria Prison — transformed into a world-class arts and heritage complex. Features contemporary art galleries, heritage exhibitions, restaurants, and a prison block you can walk through.
spots.location: 10 Hollywood Road, Central
spots.tips: Free entry but register online for peak times. The prison block is the highlight. Check for art exhibitions and guided tours. Laundry Steps are a popular photo spot.

areas.name: 上環 Sheung Wan
areas.description: A fascinating blend of old and new — traditional dried seafood shops, antique streets, and hipster cafes coexist in this historic neighbourhood west of Central.

spots.name: 海味街 Dried Seafood Street (Des Voeux Road West)
spots.description: A street lined with shops selling dried seafood — abalone, sea cucumber, shark fin, dried scallops, fish maw, and exotic ingredients. The pungent aroma, bustling atmosphere, and shop owners repacking goods create a sensory experience unique to old Hong Kong.
spots.location: Des Voeux Road West, Sheung Wan
spots.tips: Best visited in the morning when deliveries arrive. Not all shops welcome browsing — many cater to wholesale buyers. Combine with a walk to the Western Market.

spots.name: 荷李活道古董街 Hollywood Road Antique Shops
spots.description: One of the oldest streets in Hong Kong, famous for its antique shops selling Chinese ceramics, furniture, jade, calligraphy, and curios. Ranges from high-end galleries to cluttered treasure troves. The street also features street art and the famous 'Little Yellow Door' photo spot.
spots.location: Hollywood Road, Sheung Wan to Central
spots.tips: Bargaining is expected in smaller shops. Be wary of fakes in lower-end shops. High-end galleries near the Eastern end are pricier but authentic.

spots.name: 西港城 Western Market
spots.description: A beautiful Edwardian-style building (built 1906) that originally served as the North Point Ferry Pier. Now a shopping arcade housing fabric and tailor shops, craft stores, and a restaurant. The red-brick exterior is one of Hong Kong's most photographed colonial buildings.
spots.location: 323 Des Voeux Road Central, Sheung Wan
spots.tips: Free to explore. The fabric shops on the upper floors are great for custom tailoring. The building connects to Sheung Wan MTR station.

spots.name: 太平山街 Tai Ping Shan Street
spots.description: A trendy enclave of independent cafes, boutiques, art galleries, and street art tucked away on the slopes above Sheung Wan. This is where Hong Kong's bubonic plague was contained in 1894 — the area has a fascinating history. The neighbourhood (called PoHo — 'Politically incorrect' area of Hollywood Road) is the anti-LKF.
spots.location: Tai Ping Shan Street, Sheung Wan
spots.tips: Great for a leisurely morning coffee crawl. Saturday mornings are quietest. Look for the street art murals on Pound Lane and the stairs nearby.

areas.name: 灣仔 Wan Chai
areas.description: A district of dramatic contrasts — gleaming convention centres alongside preserved tong-lau tenement buildings, historic temples, and a vibrant bar scene immortalized in 'The World of Suzie Wong'.

spots.name: 藍屋 Blue House
spots.description: A stunning blue-coloured tong-lau (Chinese tenement building) built in the 1920s. One of the few remaining examples of pre-war Chinese architecture in Hong Kong. Now houses the Hong Kong House of Stories — a museum and community space celebrating Wan Chai's heritage.
spots.location: 72-74A Stone Nullah Lane, Wan Chai
spots.tips: Free entry to the museum. The adjacent Yellow House and Orange House complete the colour-themed heritage trio. Check for weekend workshops.

spots.name: 金紫荊廣場 Golden Bauhinia Square
spots.description: Home to the 6m-tall golden Bauhinia sculpture — a gift from the Chinese central government for the 1997 handover. The square hosts a daily flag-raising ceremony. Offers panoramic views of Victoria Harbour and the Kowloon skyline.
spots.location: 1 Expo Drive, Wan Chai, next to the Convention Centre
spots.tips: Flag-raising ceremony at 7:50am daily (full ceremonial at 7:50am on 1st of the month). Visit at sunset for beautiful harbour photos.

spots.name: 利東街 Lee Tung Avenue (Wedding Card Street)
spots.description: Formerly known as Wedding Card Street for its many printing shops, this pedestrianized avenue has been transformed into a European-style promenade lined with cafes, restaurants, and boutique shops. Famous for its seasonal decorative displays — especially the stunning Chinese New Year and Mid-Autumn Festival lantern installations.
spots.location: Lee Tung Avenue, Wan Chai
spots.tips: Go at night when the decorations are lit up. Great for date night dinners. Near the Wan Chai MTR station exit.

spots.name: 灣仔街市 Wan Chai Market
spots.description: A historic Bauhaus-style market building (1937) still operating as a bustling wet market. The curved facade and streamlined modern architecture contrast with the chaotic energy of fresh produce, meat, and fish stalls inside. Now a Grade III historic building.
spots.location: 264 Queen's Road East, Wan Chai
spots.tips: Visit early morning for the full wet market experience. The building's exterior is a popular Instagram spot for architecture lovers.

areas.name: 銅鑼灣 Causeway Bay
areas.description: Hong Kong's busiest shopping district — a sensory overload of neon signs, department stores, street food stalls, and crowds. Also home to Victoria Park and the Typhoon Shelter.

spots.name: 時代廣場 Times Square
spots.description: One of Hong Kong's iconic shopping malls with a massive public square that hosts the famous New Year's Eve countdown. 16 floors of shops, restaurants, a cinema, and the open-air rooftop. The square's giant TV screen and clock tower are landmarks.
spots.location: 1 Matheson Street, Causeway Bay
spots.tips: Check the calendar for free exhibitions and events in the atrium. New Year's Eve is packed but spectacular. The basement has great food options.

spots.name: 維多利亞公園 Victoria Park
spots.description: Hong Kong's largest urban park (19 hectares). Features swimming pools, tennis courts, jogging tracks, a model boat pond, and beautiful gardens. Hosts major events: the annual Hong Kong Flower Show, Chinese New Year Fairs, and the massive March 4th vigil gatherings.
spots.location: 1 Hing Fat Street, Causeway Bay
spots.tips: Great for morning tai chi viewing. Sunday is a popular day for the Filipino domestic worker gatherings. The flower show in March is world-class.

spots.name: 避風塘 Typhoon Shelter (Causeway Bay)
spots.description: A sheltered harbour where hundreds of fishing boats and yachts moor. Famous for the Typhoon Shelter seafood culture — boats serving stir-fried crab, prawns, and the legendary 'Typhoon Shelter crab' with garlic and chili. Also offers sunset views over the harbour.
spots.location: Off Causeway Bay, near Victoria Park
spots.tips: The floating restaurant experience is unique but pricey. The promenade near the Royal Hong Kong Yacht Club offers great photo opportunities at sunset.

areas.name: 南區 Southern District
areas.description: The laid-back southern coast of Hong Kong Island — beaches, fishing villages, seafood restaurants, hiking trails, and some of the city's most expensive real estate.

spots.name: 赤柱 Stanley
spots.description: A charming coastal town with a Mediterranean vibe. Features Stanley Market (a mile-long street of souvenir shops), Stanley Main Beach, Murray House (a relocated 1844 colonial building), and Blake Pier at the waterfront. The former Stanley Prison is now a museum.
spots.location: Stanley, Southern District
spots.tips: Bus 6, 6A, or 66 from Exchange Square to Stanley Village. Visit on weekdays for fewer crowds. Have lunch at one of the waterfront restaurants on the promenade.

spots.name: 淺水灣 Repulse Bay
spots.description: Hong Kong's most famous beach — a crescent of golden sand with calm waters, lifeguards, and changing facilities. The beachfront is lined with upscale restaurants and the historic Repulse Bay building. Also features the Tin Hau and Kwun Yam temples at the eastern end with colourful statues.
spots.location: Repulse Bay, Southern District
spots.tips: Bus 6 or 260 from Exchange Square. Gets crowded on weekends. The temple statues at the east end are a hidden gem — giant figures of gods and goddesses.

spots.name: 石澳 Shek O
spots.description: A picturesque fishing village turned weekend getaway, famous for its colourful houses, quiet beach, and the Dragon's Back hiking trail. Shek O Beach is a crescent of fine sand with BBQ pits. The village itself is Instagram-perfect with pastel-painted houses and narrow lanes.
spots.location: Shek O, Southern District
spots.tips: Bus 9 from Shau Kei Wan MTR. The Dragon's Back hike (starting at To Tei Wan) is one of Hong Kong's best day hikes. Try the Thai restaurant in the village.

spots.name: 香港仔 Aberdeen
spots.description: A historic fishing village and typhoon shelter that still feels like old Hong Kong. Home to hundreds of fishing boats, the Aberdeen Floating Village, and the famous Jumbo Kingdom floating restaurant (currently closed for relocation). Take a sampan ride through the harbour for an authentic view.
spots.location: Aberdeen, Southern District
spots.tips: Sampan rides cost around HK$50-100 per person. The Aberdeen Promenade offers free views. Seafood restaurants at the waterfront are excellent but tourist-priced.

spots.name: 大浪灣 Big Wave Bay
spots.description: Hong Kong's premier surfing beach with consistent swells and a relaxed bohemian vibe. The beach is backed by a small village with surfboard rentals, cafes, and BBQ pits. Also features ancient rock carvings (Bronze Age) declared a declared monument.
spots.location: Big Wave Bay, Shek O, Southern District
spots.tips: Bus 9 from Shau Kei Wan to Shek O, then 20min walk. Surf conditions best in winter. The rock carvings are behind the beach — look for the fenced area.

spots.name: 數碼港與鋼線灣 Cyberport & Telegraph Bay
spots.description: A tech campus with a beautiful waterfront promenade — one of Hong Kong's best-kept secrets. The boardwalk offers stunning sunset views over the South China Sea with very few crowds. Also has a nice beach and several cafes.
spots.location: Cyberport Road, Pok Fu Lam, Southern District
spots.tips: Bus 30 or 30X from Central. The sunset view from the Cyberport boardwalk is spectacular and uncrowded. Great for a peaceful evening walk.

areas.name: 東區 Eastern District
areas.description: The eastern side of Hong Kong Island — less touristy, with authentic local neighbourhoods, waterfront promenades, and hidden temples.

spots.name: 大坑 Tai Hang
spots.description: A charming village-like neighbourhood tucked between Causeway Bay and Happy Valley. Famous for the Tai Hang Fire Dragon Dance (Mid-Autumn Festival) where a 67m-long dragon made of straw and incense sticks parades through the streets. Also home to Michelin-starred restaurants and heritage buildings.
spots.location: Tai Hang, near Causeway Bay
spots.tips: Visit during Mid-Autumn Festival for the fire dragon. Year-round, explore the quiet streets with artisan bakeries and the historic Lin Heung Tea House.

spots.name: 鰂魚涌海濱長廊 Quarry Bay Promenade
spots.description: A beautiful waterfront walkway stretching from Quarry Bay to Shau Kei Wan. Offers stunning harbour views, gardens, a pet-friendly area, and the famous 'Montane Mansion' photo spot — a kaleidoscopic view of residential towers from the ground.
spots.location: Quarry Bay, Eastern District
spots.tips: Montane Mansion (Monte Mansion) is at 111-135 King's Road — look for the iconic Instagram shot from the central courtyard looking up.

spots.name: 香港海防博物館 Hong Kong Museum of Coastal Defence
spots.description: Housed in a former British coastal fort (1887) with original artillery batteries, underground magazines, and torpedo station. Covers 600 years of Hong Kong's coastal defence history with interactive exhibits. The views from the fort ramparts are spectacular.
spots.location: 175 Tung Hei Road, Shau Kei Wan
spots.tips: Free entry on Wednesdays. Take the escalator up instead of the steep path. The underground tunnels are fascinating. Combine with Shau Kei Wan's seafood street.

areas.name: 更多行山及景點 More Hikes & Scenery (HK Island)
areas.description: Hong Kong Island's hidden hiking trails, reservoirs, and scenic viewpoints away from the crowds.

spots.name: 龍虎山及松林廢堡 Lung Fu Shan & Pinewood Battery
spots.description: A peaceful country park on the slopes of Victoria Peak featuring a historic 1905 military battery with anti-aircraft gun emplacements and underground magazines. The trail connects to The Peak via Harlech Road. The old pillboxes and gun emplacements are atmospheric and well-preserved.
spots.location: Lung Fu Shan Country Park, Western District
spots.tips: Enter from Kotewall Road near HKU. The battery is a 20-min walk from the entrance. Combine with a Peak Circuit walk. Free entry, open 24hrs.

spots.name: 薄扶林水塘 Pok Fu Lam Reservoir
spots.description: Hong Kong's oldest reservoir (built 1863), nestled in a serene valley on the western side of HK Island. The surrounding Pok Fu Lam Country Park offers easy walking trails through mature woodland. The reservoir's stone dam and Victorian-era infrastructure are declared monuments.
spots.location: Pok Fu Lam, Southern District
spots.tips: Enter from Pok Fu Lam Road or The Peak. The circular walk is 2km and takes 30-45min. Great for a quick nature escape without leaving the city.

spots.name: 鶴咀 Cape D'Aguilar
spots.description: The southeasternmost point of Hong Kong Island — a dramatic rocky headland with a 1875 lighthouse (oldest surviving in HK), sea caves, giant wave-cut platforms, and the 'Thunder Cave' where waves boom through a sea arch. Also has a marine reserve with clear waters.
spots.location: Cape D'Aguilar, Shek O
spots.tips: Minibus 9 from Shau Kei Wan to Cape D'Aguilar Road. 45-min walk from the bus stop. The lighthouse is inside HKU's marine research station — free entry. Don't miss the whale skeleton display.

spots.name: 南朗山及海洋公園山頂 Brick Hill & Ocean Park Summit
spots.description: A 284m peak in the Southern District offering panoramic views of Aberdeen Harbour, the South China Sea, and the outlying islands. The trail passes the Ocean Park cable cars running overhead — a unique perspective. The summit has a helicopter landing pad used by the Government Flying Service.
spots.location: Brick Hill, Wong Chuk Hang
spots.tips: Start from the Ocean Park MTR station. 1.5 hours up and down. Best at sunset for the golden light over the harbour. The Ocean Park cable cars right overhead make for great photos.

spots.name: 紫羅蘭山及孖崗山 Violet Hill & The Twins
spots.description: A challenging but rewarding ridge hike connecting Violet Hill (433m) and The Twins (two steep peaks colloquially called 'The Twins'). The trail offers incredible views of Repulse Bay, Deep Water Bay, and Stanley. The descent has over 1,000 steps — a true leg workout.
spots.location: Wong Nai Chung Gap to Stanley, Southern District
spots.tips: Start from Wong Nai Chung Gap Road. 2-3 hours, very steep. The 'Thousand Steps' descent is punishing on the knees — hiking poles recommended. Best in dry weather.

spots.name: 中灣及南灣 Middle Bay & South Bay
spots.description: Two quieter alternatives to nearby Repulse Bay — smaller, more relaxed, and popular with locals rather than tourists. Middle Bay has a Lifeguard post and basic facilities. South Bay is a 5-min walk further and even quieter, with a rocky outcrop at one end.
spots.location: Between Repulse Bay and Deep Water Bay
spots.tips: Walk from Repulse Bay beach along the coastal path (15 min). Much less crowded than Repulse Bay on weekends. The snorkeling at South Bay's rocky end is decent.

spots.name: 舂坎角 Chung Hom Kok
spots.description: A small, sheltered beach on the southern coast of HK Island with clear waters and a historic WWII coastal defence gun emplacement perched on the headland. The beach is quiet even on summer weekends. The remaining gun batteries and searchlight positions are open to explore.
spots.location: Chung Hom Kok, Stanley
spots.tips: Bus 52 from Central Market or walk from Stanley. The WWII gun battery is a declared monument. The beach has no lifeguards - swim at your own risk.

areas.name: 更多古蹟及文化 More Heritage & Culture
areas.description: Colonial heritage buildings, historic churches, and cultural sites across Hong Kong Island.

spots.name: 聖約翰座堂 St John's Cathedral
spots.description: The oldest Anglican church in East Asia (built 1849) and the seat of the Archbishop of Hong Kong. This neo-Gothic cathedral has survived both World Wars, Japanese occupation (when it was used as a clubhouse), and countless typhoons. The stained glass windows and peace garden are highlights.
spots.location: 4 Garden Road, Central
spots.tips: Free entry. Open daily 7am-6pm. The mid-day organ recital (Wednesdays) is excellent. The cathedral grounds are a peaceful oasis in the heart of Central.

spots.name: 香港大學 Main Building The University of Hong Kong
spots.description: The oldest university in Hong Kong (founded 1911), with its iconic red-brick Edwardian Baroque main building (Loke Yew Hall) and the striking Centennial Campus. The university's museum (UMAG) has excellent Chinese art collections. The campus on Pok Fu Lam Road offers panoramic views.
spots.location: Pok Fu Lam Road, Central & Western District
spots.tips: The main building is a declared monument. Visit the UMAG museum (free). The campus cafes are great for a break. Take the MTR to HKU Station for direct access.

spots.name: 香港動植物公園 Hong Kong Zoological & Botanical Gardens
spots.description: The oldest public park in Hong Kong (established 1871), home to a small zoo with primates, flamingos, and exotic birds. The botanical section features a stunning collection of rare plants, a fountain terrace, and a 1920s bandstand. The park sits on the slopes of Government Hill with views over Central.
spots.location: Albany Road, Central
spots.tips: Free entry. Open 5am-10pm. The primate enclosure has orangutans and gibbons. Combine with a walk to the nearby Peak Tram terminus.

spots.name: 香港公園 Hong Kong Park
spots.description: A 8-hectare modern urban park built on the former Victoria Barracks. Features a spectacular aviary (the largest in SE Asia), a tai chi garden, visual arts centre, and the Flagstaff House Museum of Tea Ware (1846 — the oldest colonial building still standing in HK).
spots.location: 19 Cotton Tree Drive, Admiralty
spots.tips: Free entry to the park. The aviary is a highlight — walk through a netted rainforest canopy at ground level. The Museum of Tea Ware in Flagstaff House is free on Wednesdays.

spots.name: 香港大學美術博物館 UMAG
spots.description: Hong Kong's oldest museum (founded 1953), housed in the 1930s Fung Ping Shan Building. The collection spans 4,000+ pieces of Chinese ceramics, porcelain, bronzes, and paintings. The museum also hosts rotating contemporary art exhibitions. A hidden cultural treasure on the HKU campus.
spots.location: 90 Bonham Road, Pok Fu Lam
spots.tips: Free entry. Open Tue-Sat 9:30am-6pm, Sun 1-6pm. The ceramics collection is world-class. Combine with a campus walk — the main building is stunning.

kowloon.name: 九龍 Kowloon
kowloon.description: The bustling peninsula opposite Hong Kong Island — a sensory explosion of neon lights, street markets, dim sum palaces, and some of the most vibrant urban landscapes on Earth.

areas.name: 尖沙咀 Tsim Sha Tsui
areas.description: The most tourist-friendly district in Kowloon — world-class museums, the harbour promenade, luxury shopping, and the famous Star Ferry terminal.

spots.name: 維多利亞港及星光大道 Victoria Harbour & Avenue of Stars
spots.name_cn: 維多利亞港及星光大道
spots.description: One of the most famous harbour views in the world. The Avenue of Stars is the TST promenade lined with handprints of Hong Kong movie stars (Bruce Lee, Jackie Chan, Wong Kar-wai). Evening 'A Symphony of Lights' show illuminates both sides of the harbour.
spots.location: Tsim Sha Tsui Promenade, Salisbury Road
spots.tips: Best views of the Hong Kong Island skyline. The Symphony of Lights show starts at 8pm daily. Arrive by 7:30pm for a good spot. The Bruce Lee statue is the most photographed spot.

spots.name: 香港文化中心 Hong Kong Cultural Centre
spots.description: A striking curved building housing the Concert Hall, Grand Theatre, and Studio Theatre. Hosts world-class performances by the Hong Kong Philharmonic, Chinese opera, ballet, and international artists. The adjacent Hong Kong Space Museum is instantly recognizable by its dome-shaped planetarium.
spots.location: 10 Salisbury Road, Tsim Sha Tsui
spots.tips: Check the performance schedule in advance. The building's architecture is worth photographing even if you don't attend a show. Free exhibitions often in the foyer.

spots.name: 鐘樓 Clock Tower
spots.description: The only remaining structure of the original Kowloon-Canton Railway terminus (1915). This 44m-high clock tower is a declared monument and one of Hong Kong's most photographed landmarks. It stands at the Star Ferry pier as a gateway to the harbour.
spots.location: Salisbury Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, near Star Ferry
spots.tips: The clock tower is illuminated at night. Best photographed from across the harbour or from the Star Ferry. Combine with a walk along the TST promenade.

spots.name: 香港藝術館 Hong Kong Museum of Art
spots.description: Houses an extensive collection of Chinese art, calligraphy, antiquities, and Hong Kong contemporary art. The renovated museum (reopened 2019) features stunning harbour-view windows and world-class exhibitions spanning 4,000 years of Chinese art.
spots.location: 10 Salisbury Road, Tsim Sha Tsui
spots.tips: Free entry to permanent exhibitions. The rooftop garden offers a fantastic harbour view. Allow 2-3 hours.

spots.name: K11 MUSEA
spots.description: A stunning 'museum-retail' concept mall designed by 100 international architects and artists. Features a dramatic curved facade, the 'Opera Theatre' central atrium with waterfall, luxury boutiques, art installations, and the MoMA Design Store. The Gold Ball sculpture is Insta-famous.
spots.location: 18 Salisbury Road, Tsim Sha Tsui
spots.tips: Go early (opens 10am) for empty photo opportunities at the Opera Theatre. The 7th-floor rooftop garden offers great harbour views.

spots.name: 海港城 Harbour City
spots.description: Hong Kong's largest shopping mall — a sprawling complex of over 450 shops, 50 restaurants, a cinema, and art spaces. Connects Ocean Terminal, Ocean Centre, and Gateway Arcade. The rooftop car park offers one of the best free harbour views in TST.
spots.location: 3-27 Canton Road, Tsim Sha Tsui
spots.tips: Visit the rooftop car park at Ocean Terminal for amazing sunset photos. The LCX section has trendy Japanese/Korean brands. Weekends are packed.

spots.name: 1881 Heritage
spots.description: The former Marine Police Headquarters (1881) — a Victorian Gothic building transformed into a luxury shopping and dining complex. Features the original turret, stable block, signal tower, and an open-air courtyard. The Christmas decorations are legendary.
spots.location: 2A Canton Road, Tsim Sha Tsui
spots.tips: The courtyard and clock tower are free to explore. The Christmas display is one of Hong Kong's best. Go at night when the building is dramatically lit.

areas.name: 佐敦及油麻地 Jordan & Yau Ma Tei
areas.description: The heart of old Kowloon — night markets, temples, neon signs, and the gritty, authentic energy that Hong Kong is famous for.

spots.name: 廟街夜市 Temple Street Night Market
spots.description: Hong Kong's most famous night market — a sensory overload of neon-lit stalls selling clothes, watches, electronics, antiques, and souvenirs. Fortune tellers, street performers, dai pai dong (open-air food stalls), and the Tin Hau Temple at its heart. The market is chaotic, loud, and utterly unforgettable.
spots.location: Temple Street, Jordan to Yau Ma Tei
spots.tips: Best visited after 7pm when fully active. Bargain hard (start at 30-40% of asking price). Try the claypot rice and curry fish balls at the dai pai dong. Watch for pickpockets.

spots.name: 廟街 Tin Hau Temple (Yau Ma Tei)
spots.description: Built in 1865, this is the largest of Hong Kong's Tin Hau temples and the namesake of Temple Street. A peaceful oasis amid the market chaos. The complex includes a See Yee Koon (community hall) and a former school. The temple's incense coils and carved roof ridges are exquisite.
spots.location: Market Street & Temple Street, Yau Ma Tei
spots.tips: Free entry. Open daily 8am-5pm. Visit during the day when the market is quiet for a more spiritual experience.

spots.name: 玉器市場 Jade Market
spots.description: A covered market with over 400 stalls selling jade jewellery, ornaments, and raw jade stones. Open since the 1960s. Even if you're not buying, the variety of green hues and the lively bargaining atmosphere make it worth a visit.
spots.location: Kansu Street & Battery Street, Yau Ma Tei
spots.tips: Open daily 10am-5pm. Genuine jade is expensive — learn the basics of spotting fakes. The adjacent Yau Ma Tei Fruit Market (1913) is worth a look for the historic buildings.

spots.name: 油麻地果欄 Yau Ma Tei Fruit Market
spots.description: A historic fruit wholesale market housed in single-storey pre-war buildings (1913). The market comes alive in the dead of night (midnight to dawn) when trucks unload fresh fruit from around the world. The Art Deco architecture has made it a favourite spot for photographers and film shoots.
spots.location: Waterloo Road & Reclamation Street, Yau Ma Tei
spots.tips: Visit around 3-5am for the full wholesale experience. During the day it's quiet but the colonial architecture is still visible. Photography enthusiasts love this place.

areas.name: 旺角 Mong Kok
areas.description: The densest neighbourhood on Earth (130,000 people per km²) — a maze of themed markets, neon signs, and relentless energy. The ultimate expression of Hong Kong's urban intensity.

spots.name: 女人街 Ladies' Market (Tung Choi Street)
spots.description: A 1km-long street market packed with stalls selling clothing, accessories, handbags, cosmetics, and souvenirs at bargain prices. Despite the name, men's items are sold too. The market is covered by blue tarpaulins, creating a colourful canopy.
spots.location: Tung Choi Street, Mong Kok
spots.tips: Open daily 12pm-11:30pm. Bargain aggressively. Quality is generally low — it's about the experience. Go around 4-6pm for the best energy without peak crowds.

spots.name: 金魚街 Goldfish Market (Tung Choi Street North)
spots.description: A bizarre and fascinating street where pet shops display goldfish and tropical fish in plastic bags hanging from storefronts — creating a wall of floating fish. Sells aquarium fish, pets, and supplies. One of Hong Kong's most Instagrammed streets.
spots.location: Tung Choi Street (North section), Mong Kok
spots.tips: Best photographed in the afternoon when the light catches the bags. Unusual and free to wander. Combine with the nearby Flower Market.

spots.name: 花墟道 Flower Market
spots.description: A vibrant flower market with over 100 shops selling fresh-cut flowers, potted plants, bonsai, and gardening supplies. The explosion of colour and fragrance is a welcome contrast to the urban chaos of Mong Kok. Particularly stunning during Chinese New Year.
spots.location: Flower Market Road, Prince Edward / Mong Kok
spots.tips: Open daily 7am-7pm. Prices drop in the late afternoon. During Chinese New Year week, the market stays open late and is spectacularly decorated.

spots.name: 波鞋街 Sneaker Street (Fa Yuen Street)
spots.description: A street dedicated entirely to sports shoes and sneakers — over 50 shops selling every brand imaginable, from Nike and Adidas to rare limited editions. The street is lined with shoes hanging overhead on racks. A pilgrimage site for sneakerheads.
spots.location: Fa Yuen Street, Mong Kok
spots.tips: Genuine products but watch for parallel imports (non-HK warranty). Limited edition releases have queues. Bargaining is limited in brand-name stores.

spots.name: 旺角街市 Mong Kok Market Complex
spots.description: The ultimate local wet market experience — a multi-storey complex with fresh produce, meat, seafood, cooked food, and dry goods. The ground-floor street market spills onto the sidewalks with vendors hawking everything from vegetables to live frogs.
spots.location: Mong Kok Road & Fa Yuen Street
spots.tips: Go early morning for the full experience. Try the cooked food stalls on the upper floors for cheap, authentic Hong Kong-style meals.

spots.name: 西洋菜南街 Sai Yeung Choi Street South
spots.description: Mong Kok's main pedestrian shopping street — a carnival of electronics stores, cosmetics shops, street performers, political protesters, and the famous neon sign jungle. On weekends, the street is closed to traffic and becomes a pedestrian-only zone.
spots.location: Sai Yeung Choi Street South, Mong Kok
spots.tips: The neon signs are best photographed from the footbridges. Watch for pickpockets in crowds. Street performers range from musicians to political activists.

areas.name: 深水埗 Sham Shui Po
areas.description: One of Hong Kong's oldest and most authentic neighbourhoods — a treasure trove of vintage electronics, fabric markets, street food, and a rapidly emerging arts scene.

spots.name: 黃金電腦商場 Golden Computer Centre
spots.description: The mecca of computer hardware in Hong Kong — a multi-level shopping centre packed with stalls selling every conceivable component, peripheral, and gadget at bargain prices. If it plugs into a computer, it's sold here.
spots.location: 146-152 Fuk Wa Street, Sham Shui Po
spots.tips: Compare prices across multiple stalls. Be wary of grey-market goods. Cash is preferred. The adjacent Golden Computer Arcade has more gaming and console gear.

spots.name: 鴨寮街 Apliu Street Flea Market
spots.description: Hong Kong's legendary flea market for electronics, second-hand goods, and vintage treasures. Stalls sprawl across the street selling everything from vintage audio equipment and cameras to obscure electronic components. A paradise for tinkerers, collectors, and bargain hunters.
spots.location: Apliu Street, Sham Shui Po
spots.tips: Open noon-10pm. Best browsing in the afternoon. Bring cash and bargain hard. Radio enthusiasts will find rare components. Check vendor reputation before buying expensive vintage items.

spots.name: 北河街街市 Pei Ho Street Market
spots.description: One of Hong Kong's most intense wet markets — a chaotic, colourful, and utterly authentic local food market. Live seafood, fresh produce, butchers, tofu makers, and cooked food stalls spill onto the street. A photographer's dream of old Hong Kong.
spots.location: Pei Ho Street, Sham Shui Po
spots.tips: Go early morning (6-9am) for the busiest action. The tofu pudding stall at the corner is a local institution. Photography is welcome but ask permission for close-ups of vendors.

spots.name: 美荷樓 Mei Ho House
spots.description: A beautifully preserved example of a 1950s H-shaped public housing block — now a museum and youth hostel. The Heritage Museum recreates the living conditions of early public housing tenants with full-scale replicas of flats from the 1950s-1970s. A poignant window into Hong Kong's social history.
spots.location: 70 Tai Po Road, Sham Shui Po (near Shek Kip Mei MTR)
spots.tips: Free entry to the museum. The rooftop cafe has great views. Book in advance for the hostel. Allow 1 hour for the museum.

spots.name: 欽州街小販市場 Kam Tong Street Hawker Market
spots.description: A hidden gem — a traditional hawker bazaar with stalls selling vintage clothing, handcrafted goods, Chinese herbs, and second-hand treasures. Less touristy than Temple Street, more authentic. The fabric section is particularly vibrant.
spots.location: Kam Tong Street, Sham Shui Po
spots.tips: Best on weekends. The fabric market is great for DIY crafters. Combine with a visit to the nearby Sam Tai Tsuen Temple.

areas.name: 九龍城 Kowloon City
areas.description: A historic district frozen in time — famous for the demolished Kowloon Walled City, incredible Thai food, and the remnants of old Hong Kong's low-rise architecture.

spots.name: 九龍寨城公園 Kowloon Walled City Park
spots.description: Built on the site of the infamous Kowloon Walled City — once the most densely populated place on Earth (33,000 people in 2.6 hectares). The 'city of darkness' was demolished in 1993-94 and replaced with a serene Jiangnan-style garden. The park preserves the original yamen (administrative building), remnants of the wall, and a scale model of the original walled city.
spots.location: Tung Tsing Road, Kowloon City
spots.tips: Free entry, open 6:30am-11pm. Don't miss the scale model showing how the walled city looked — it's mind-boggling. The garden follows traditional Chinese landscape design principles.

spots.name: 九龍城 Thai Food District
spots.description: Kowloon City is Hong Kong's 'Little Thailand' — over 30 authentic Thai restaurants, grocery stores, and dessert shops line the streets. The Thai community has been here since the 1970s, serving some of the best Thai food outside Bangkok. Hao Hao and Chilli Thai are legendary.
spots.location: Lung Kong Road & Nam Kok Road, Kowloon City
spots.tips: Hao Hao Restaurant (40-42 Nam Kok Road) is the most famous. Try the pad thai, green curry, and mango sticky rice. Many shops also sell authentic Thai ingredients and snacks.

spots.name: 衙前圍村 Nga Tsin Wai Village
spots.description: A rare surviving walled village in the heart of urban Kowloon — over 600 years old. The village was originally surrounded by walls with a moat. Today, the narrow alleys, ancestral halls, and traditional houses offer a glimpse of pre-colonial Hong Kong life, surrounded by towering developments.
spots.location: Nga Tsin Wai Road, Kowloon City
spots.tips: Free to walk through. The village is partially demolished for redevelopment — visit while it still exists. The nearby Tung Tsing Road has great cha chaan tengs (HK-style cafes).

areas.name: 鯉魚門及觀塘 Lei Yue Mun & Kwun Tong
areas.description: The eastern coast of Kowloon — a seafood village frozen in time, and a former industrial district transformed into an arts hub.

spots.name: 鯉魚門 Lei Yue Mun Seafood Village
spots.description: A charming fishing village turned seafood paradise. Choose live fish, prawns, crabs, and lobsters from the fish tanks, then have them cooked at one of the many waterfront restaurants. The narrow alley is lined with seafood tanks and dried seafood shops. The village also has a lighthouse, Tin Hau Temple, and a short hiking trail.
spots.location: Lei Yue Mun, Yau Tong, Kowloon
spots.tips: Take MTR to Yau Tong, then 15min walk. Seafood is market price — agree on price before ordering. Popular restaurants include Tai Fook and Fat Kee. Best at sunset.

spots.name: 觀塘海濱長廊 Kwun Tong Promenade
spots.description: A beautifully designed waterfront walkway on the former Kwun Tong cargo pier. Features a striking metallic tree sculpture, a public square, graffiti art from local artists, and stunning views of the harbour and the Tseung Kwan O bridge. A peaceful escape from the industrial area.
spots.location: Hoi Yuen Road, Kwun Tong
spots.tips: Best at sunset. The metallic 'Wind Tree' sculpture is the iconic photo spot. The nearby waterfront restaurants are good for dinner. Combine with a visit to the artist lofts.

spots.name: 觀塘工業區藝術空間 Kwun Tong Industrial Art Spaces
spots.description: Abandoned industrial buildings in Kwun Tong have been transformed into artist studios, galleries, and creative spaces. The 'Hidden Agenda' live music venue, the 'Observe' gallery, and numerous independent studios host exhibitions, workshops, and performances. A vibrant underground arts scene.
spots.location: Various industrial buildings, Kwun Tong
spots.tips: Check gallery opening hours in advance — many are appointment-only. The annual 'Kwun Tong Arts Festival' (December) is the best time to visit.

areas.name: 更多景點 More Attractions (Kowloon)
areas.description: Kowloon's hiking peaks, heritage sites, and scenic spots that most visitors miss.

spots.name: 獅子山 Lion Rock
spots.description: Hong Kong's most iconic peak (495m) — named for its shape resembling a crouching lion. The summit offers arguably the best view of Hong Kong: the entire Kowloon peninsula, Victoria Harbour, and Hong Kong Island. Lion Rock Country Park surrounds it with extensive hiking trails. A symbol of the 'Hong Kong spirit'.
spots.location: Lion Rock Country Park, Kowloon
spots.tips: Start from Wong Tai Sin MTR or the Lion Rock Park entrance. 2-3 hours return. The summit is exposed — avoid in thunderstorms. Best at sunrise for epic views over the city.

spots.name: 飛鵝山 Kowloon Peak (Fei Ngo Shan)
spots.description: The highest peak in Kowloon (602m), offering a bird's-eye view of the entire territory from Sai Kung to Tsuen Wan. The summit is accessible by road (closed to public vehicles), making it popular for sunset photography. The 'Suicide Trail' is an infamous steep ridge hike.
spots.location: Fei Ngo Shan Road, Clear Water Bay
spots.tips: Taxi to the top from Choi Hung MTR (~HK$60). The sunset view is the best in Kowloon. The 'Suicide Trail' is extremely dangerous — do NOT attempt it without proper gear and experience.

spots.name: 金山郊野公園 Kam Shan Country Park (Monkey Mountain)
spots.description: Famous for its large population of wild macaques — hundreds of monkeys roam freely along the Golden Hill hiking trail. The park also features four reservoirs (the 'Four Hills' of Kam Shan) and WWII-era pillboxes. The monkeys are the main attraction but beware — they WILL steal your food.
spots.location: Kam Shan, Sha Tin / Kowloon border
spots.tips: Enter from Shek Lei Pui Reservoir. DO NOT carry visible food — the monkeys will grab it. Keep distance and don't make eye contact. Best visited in the morning when monkeys are most active.

spots.name: 鯉魚門度假村及砲台 Lei Yue Mun Fort & Holiday Camp
spots.description: A 19th-century British coastal defence fort on the Kowloon side of the Lei Yue Mun channel, now a government holiday camp. The original fortifications — gun batteries, barracks, underground magazines — are remarkably well-preserved and open for exploration. The view across the channel to HK Island is stunning.
spots.location: Lei Yue Mun, Yau Tong
spots.tips: Open only on select public open days or by booking. The military cemetery next door is a solemn but fascinating piece of HK history. Combine with a seafood meal in Lei Yue Mun village.

new_territories.name: 新界 New Territories
new_territories.description: The largest region of Hong Kong — a vast expanse of country parks, ancient walled villages, wetlands, hiking trails, and traditional rural life that most tourists never see.

areas.name: 西貢 Sai Kung
areas.description: Called the 'Back Garden of Hong Kong' — a stunning area of pristine beaches, volcanic rock formations, sea caves, and a charming fishing town with the best seafood in the territory.

spots.name: 西貢市中心 Sai Kung Town
spots.description: A charming fishing town with a picturesque waterfront promenade lined with seafood restaurants displaying live catch. The weekend market sells handicrafts, antiques, and street food. The pier is the departure point for boats to outlying islands and remote beaches.
spots.location: Sai Kung Town, Sai Kung District
spots.tips: Seafood restaurants on the promenade are excellent but pricier — try the side streets for better value. Take a kaito (ferry) to Sharp Island for a day trip.

spots.name: 大浪灣 Tai Long Wan (Big Wave Bay, Sai Kung)
spots.description: Not to be confused with the Big Wave Bay on HK Island — this is a stunning stretch of four consecutive beaches on the eastern coast of the Sai Kung Peninsula: Sai Wan, Ham Tin, Tai Wan, and Tung Wan. Crystal clear waters, golden sand, and dramatic headlands. Considered Hong Kong's most beautiful coastline.
spots.location: Sai Kung East Country Park
spots.tips: Accessible by hiking the MacLehose Trail Stage 2 (2.5h from Pak Tam Au) or by speedboat from Sai Kung (20min, ~HK$150/person round trip). Bring water and sun protection.

spots.name: 橋嘴島 Sharp Island (Kiu Tsui)
spots.description: A small island connected to Sai Kung by a narrow sand spit (tombolo) that appears at low tide — Hong Kong's own 'Moses Bridge'. Has a beautiful beach, hiking trails, and fascinating volcanic rock formations including the 'pineapple bun' rocks.
spots.location: Off Sai Kung Town (10min kaito ferry)
spots.tips: Check tide times before crossing the tombolo. Avoid mid-day summer heat. The kaito ferry runs from Sai Kung pier multiple times daily.

spots.name: 萬宜水庫 High Island Reservoir
spots.description: An engineering marvel — a massive freshwater reservoir formed by damming the sea with two giant rock-fill dams. The surrounding area is part of the Hong Kong UNESCO Global Geopark, featuring spectacular hexagonal volcanic rock columns, sea caves, and the famous 'Dragon's Back' rock formation.
spots.location: Sai Kung East Country Park
spots.tips: The East Dam is accessible by taxi from Sai Kung (about HK$120). Walk along the dam to see the giant concrete dolosse and the hexagonal columns on the sea wall. Combine with a hike to the nearby waterfalls.

spots.name: 鹽田仔 Yim Tin Tsai
spots.description: A tiny island in Sai Kung Harbour with a fascinating history — a Hakka village established 300 years ago that produced salt (hence the name 'Little Salt Field'). Abandoned in 1998, the village has been revived with a restored salt pan, a Catholic church (1866), and a heritage museum. Won a UNESCO heritage award.
spots.location: Sai Kung Harbour (15min kaito from Sai Kung pier)
spots.tips: Weekend kaitos run regularly. The salt-making demonstration is fascinating. The church is a beautiful example of vernacular architecture.

spots.name: 滘西洲 Kau Sai Chau
spots.description: A large island in Sai Kung known for its public golf course (the only one in HK run by a charity), but also featuring beautiful hiking trails, a Tin Hau Temple, and quiet beaches. The island is mostly uninhabited and covered in woodland.
spots.location: Sai Kung Harbour (kaito from Sai Kung pier)
spots.tips: The golf course is affordable by HK standards. Non-golfers can hike the trails. The public ferry runs several times daily.

areas.name: 大嶼山 Lantau Island
areas.description: Hong Kong's largest island — twice the size of Hong Kong Island — home to the Big Buddha, Disneyland, the fishing village of Tai O, and miles of pristine hiking trails.

spots.name: 天壇大佛及寶蓮禪寺 Tian Tan Buddha & Po Lin Monastery
spots.description: The world's tallest outdoor seated bronze Buddha (34m, 250 tonnes), sitting majestically on a mountaintop at Ngong Ping. Climb 268 steps to stand at the Buddha's feet for panoramic views. The adjacent Po Lin Monastery (built 1924) is a major Buddhist centre with ornate temples, vegetarian dining, and serene gardens.
spots.location: Ngong Ping, Lantau Island
spots.tips: Visit on a clear day — the Buddha is often shrouded in cloud. The Ngong Ping 360 cable car (25min from Tung Chung) offers spectacular views. The vegetarian lunch at Po Lin Monastery is a unique experience.

spots.name: 昂坪360 Ngong Ping 360 Cable Car
spots.description: A 5.7km cable car journey from Tung Chung to Ngong Ping, offering breathtaking 360-degree views of the North Lantau Country Park, the South China Sea, the airport, and the Big Buddha. The Crystal Cabin (glass-bottom) adds an extra thrill.
spots.location: Tung Chung, Lantau Island (adjacent to Tung Chung MTR)
spots.tips: Book online to avoid long queues. Crystal Cabin is worth the upgrade. Best visibility in the morning. The ride takes about 25 minutes each way.

spots.name: 大澳 Tai O Fishing Village
spots.description: The 'Venice of Hong Kong' — a traditional fishing village built on stilts over the tidal flats. Famous for its stilt houses, narrow alleyways, dried seafood, and boat tours through the waterways where pink dolphins can sometimes be spotted. Tai O is one of the last remaining examples of traditional fishing village culture in Hong Kong.
spots.location: Tai O, Lantau Island
spots.tips: Take bus 21 from Ngong Ping (after visiting the Buddha) — a 20min scenic ride. Try the shrimp paste (ha jeung) and egg waffle with sesame. Take a boat tour for the stilt house views (negotiate price first).

spots.name: 大澳文物酒店 Tai O Heritage Hotel
spots.description: A beautifully restored 1902 colonial police station turned boutique hotel and restaurant. The building's gun turrets, arched verandas, and thick granite walls have been preserved. The glass-roofed restaurant serves excellent fusion cuisine with views over the South China Sea.
spots.location: Shek Tsai Po Street, Tai O, Lantau
spots.tips: Free to visit the public areas and museum room. The afternoon tea at the Tai O Lookout restaurant is lovely. Book Sunday brunch in advance.

spots.name: 香港迪士尼樂園 Hong Kong Disneyland
spots.description: The smallest Disney resort but with unique attractions you won't find elsewhere — Mystic Manor, the Mystic Point (exclusive to HK), and the Lantau-themed 'Adventureland'. Seven themed lands, including the newest 'World of Frozen' (2023). Less crowded than other Disney parks.
spots.location: Penny's Bay, Lantau Island
spots.tips: Go on weekdays for the shortest queues. Download the HK Disney app for wait times. Mystic Manor is a must-ride — it's the best dark ride in any Disney park.

spots.name: 貝澳沙灘 Pui O Beach
spots.description: A beautiful, uncrowded beach on the southern coast of Lantau — golden sand, calm waters, and a backdrop of verdant hills. The adjacent Pui O hamlet has a few excellent Thai restaurants and a laid-back vibe. The beach is a designated campsite with facilities.
spots.location: Pui O, Lantau Island
spots.tips: Bus 3M or A35 from Tung Chung. Great for swimming and camping. The Thai restaurant on the main road (Pui O Thai) is fantastic. Camping permits required for the official site.

spots.name: 長沙沙灘 Cheung Sha Beach
spots.description: The longest beach in Hong Kong (3km of golden sand on Lantau's southern coast). Divided into Upper Cheung Sha and Lower Cheung Sha, both with excellent swimming. The beach is backed by small cafes, surf shops, and the popular 'The Stoep' restaurant — a South African-style beach bar.
spots.location: Cheung Sha, Lantau Island
spots.tips: Bus 3M or A35 from Tung Chung. The Stoep serves great pizza and beer. Surfing is possible in winter. Much quieter than HK Island beaches.

spots.name: 鳳凰山 Lantau Peak (Fung Wong Shan)
spots.description: The second-highest peak in Hong Kong (934m). Famous for sunrise hikes — watching the sun rise above the clouds from the top is a bucket-list experience. The trail starts from Tung Chung or Ngong Ping and takes about 2-3 hours. The summit offers 360-degree views of Lantau and the South China Sea.
spots.location: Lantau South Country Park
spots.tips: Start the hike at 3-4am for sunrise. Bring a torch and warm layers (summit is cool even in summer). The descent via the Wisdom Path is stunning. Combine with a visit to the Big Buddha.

spots.name: 愉景灣 Discovery Bay
spots.description: A unique expatriate community on Lantau's northeastern coast — cars are banned, residents get around by golf cart. The result is a tranquil, pedestrian-friendly beachside town with Mediterranean architecture, a white sand beach (the only one on Lantau's north side), waterfront dining, and a resort atmosphere.
spots.location: Discovery Bay, Lantau Island
spots.tips: Reachable by 25-min ferry from Central Pier 3 or bus DB01R from Tung Chung. The DB Plaza has the best restaurants. The beach is artificial but well-maintained. Great for a relaxed family day out.

spots.name: 梅窩 Mui Wo
spots.description: The main town on Lantau's eastern coast — a laid-back community with a silver-sand beach, a historic pier, a Tin Hau Temple (built 1740), and the starting point for the famous 'Silvermine Cave' — an abandoned silver mine. The ferry from Central takes just 35 minutes.
spots.location: Mui Wo, Lantau Island
spots.tips: Ferry from Central Pier 6 (35-55min). Rent a bike to explore the area. The Silvermine Cave is small but historically interesting. The China Bear pub serves fish and chips.

spots.name: 分流 Fan Lau
spots.description: The southwestern tip of Lantau — one of Hong Kong's most remote and wild places. Features a 19th-century Qing dynasty fort, abandoned villages, a 5,000-year-old Neolithic site, and dramatic coastal scenery. The hike there offers panoramic views of the Pearl River Delta and Macau on clear days.
spots.location: Fan Lau, Lantau South Country Park
spots.tips: Hard hike: 4-5 hours return from Shek Pik. Bring 3L of water per person. The old fort and abandoned village are hauntingly beautiful. Extremely remote — no shops or facilities.

spots.name: 東涌 Tung Chung
spots.description: The gateway to Lantau — a rapidly developing new town with the Tung Chung Fort (1817, built by the Qing to defend against opium smugglers), the Ngong Ping 360 cable car terminal, and a massive outlet mall (Citygate Outlets). The Tung Chung River and coastal boardwalk offer peaceful walks.
spots.location: Tung Chung, Lantau Island
spots.tips: The old Tung Chung Fort is free and worth a quick visit. Citygate Outlets has good deals on branded goods. The walk along the Tung Chung waterfront to the fish pond is a nice evening activity.

areas.name: 離島 Outlying Islands
areas.description: The smaller islands scattered around Hong Kong — each with its own character, from bustling fishing communities to completely uninhabited wilderness.

spots.name: 長洲 Cheung Chau
spots.description: A dumbbell-shaped island packed with character — Hong Kong's most popular outlying island. Famous for the Bun Festival (Cheung Chau Jiao Festival, April/May) with its 'bun snatching' competition, parade of the 'floating children' on stilts, and three days of Taoist ceremonies. Year-round attractions include the fishing village, harbour, beaches (Tung Wan, Kwun Yam Wan), the Mini Great Wall hiking trail, rock carvings, and seafood restaurants.
spots.location: Cheung Chau Island (40min fast ferry from Central Pier 5)
spots.tips: Try the famous mango mochi, fish balls, and giant squid at the harbourfront. Take the Mini Great Wall hike for amazing coastal views. The Bun Festival is incredible but the island is jam-packed.

spots.name: 南丫島 Lamma Island
spots.description: Hong Kong's 'hippie island' — car-free, laid-back, and dotted with alternative-lifestyle communities, seafood restaurants, and hiking trails. The main settlements are Yung Shue Wan (north) and Sok Kwu Wan (south), connected by a scenic 1-hour Family Trail passing beaches, a former power station (the three towering chimneys are iconic), and the kampung village of Tung O with its Tin Hau Temple.
spots.location: Lamma Island (25min ferry from Central Pier 4 to Yung Shue Wan, or 20min to Sok Kwu Wan)
spots.tips: The Rainbow Seafood Restaurant in Sok Kwu Wan is legendary. Try the organic bakery in Yung Shue Wan. Hike from Yung Shue Wan to Sok Kwu Wan (1h) and take the ferry back.

spots.name: 坪洲 Peng Chau
spots.description: A tiny, quiet island (less than 1km²) with a charming village atmosphere, abandoned factory buildings (remnants of its industrial past), a Finger Hill hiking trail, and the Peng Chau Fisherfolk Village. The island feels like a step back in time — bicycles are the main transport, and life moves slowly.
spots.location: Peng Chau Island (30min ferry from Central Pier 6)
spots.tips: Rent a bicycle to explore the whole island in 1-2 hours. The abandoned factories make for atmospheric photography. The seafood restaurants on the waterfront are cheaper than Lamma.

spots.name: 蒲台島 Po Toi Island
spots.description: Hong Kong's southernmost island — a windswept, wild landscape of bizarre granite rock formations ('Maid with Baby', 'Tortoise climbing up the mountain', 'Monk Rock'), ancient rock carvings (declared monument, 3,000 years old), and a historic lighthouse (Po Toi Lighthouse, 1910). Famous for its seaweed noodles and stunning coastal hikes.
spots.location: Po Toi Island (1h ferry from Aberdeen on weekends/holidays only)
spots.tips: Only accessible on weekends and public holidays. The 'Ming Kee Seafood Restaurant' serves excellent seaweed noodles and fried squid. The lighthouse is the southernmost point of Hong Kong.

spots.name: 東平洲 Tung Ping Chau
spots.description: Hong Kong's most remote inhabited island — a UNESCO Global Geopark site famous for its spectacular sedimentary rock formations (layer-cake cliffs, sea caves, and wave-cut platforms). The island is flat (only 20m at its highest), ringed by a 6km hiking trail that takes 2-3 hours. Abandoned Hakka villages add cultural interest.
spots.location: Tung Ping Chau (1.5h ferry from Ma Liu Shui pier, weekends only)
spots.tips: Weekends and public holidays only. The ferry departs at 9am and returns at 5:15pm — do NOT miss the return boat. Bring all food and water. The rock formations are most spectacular at low tide.

spots.name: 塔門 Tap Mun (Grass Island)
spots.description: A peaceful island known for its rolling green hills where wild cows and buffalo graze freely. The hilltop offers panoramic views of the surrounding waters. A short hiking trail circles the island (1-2 hours), passing a Tin Hau Temple, a fishing village, and stunning coastal cliffs. The seafood at the village is excellent.
spots.location: Tap Mun (ferry from Wong Shek Pier in Sai Kung, or from Ma Liu Shui)
spots.tips: The cows are wild — do not feed them. The seafood restaurant 'New Hon Kee' is excellent. The sunset from the hilltop is stunning. Camping is allowed on the grass slopes.

spots.name: 東龍洲 Tung Lung Chau
spots.description: An uninhabited island known for its ancient rock carvings (3,000 years old, declared monument), a 17th-century Qing dynasty fort, and excellent rock climbing on the sea cliffs. The island has a campsite, a few abandoned villages, and a circular hiking trail with spectacular coastal scenery.
spots.location: Tung Lung Chau (ferry from Sai Wan Ho or Sam Ka Tsuen, weekends only)
spots.tips: Rock climbing routes are world-class — bring your own gear. The fort is free to explore. The ferry runs only on weekends and public holidays. Take all supplies with you.

spots.name: 吉澳 Kat O (Crooked Island)
spots.description: A remote island in the northeastern waters, part of the UNESCO Global Geopark. The Hakka fishing village has a fascinating history — over 40 clans settled here for the sheltered harbour. Features a Tin Hau Temple (1763), a 'Love Stone' (a natural heart-shaped rock hole), and peaceful hiking. The island was a major pearl trading post in the Ming dynasty.
spots.location: Kat O (ferry from Ma Liu Shui on weekends — inquire at the pier)
spots.tips: Very remote — no ATMs, limited shops. The Love Stone is a popular photo spot. The island's story is incredibly rich — ask a local. Visit the Fong Yuet Nam Hing Chinese Medicine Hall (100+ years old).

areas.name: 沙田 Sha Tin
areas.description: A major new town in the New Territories — home to the Hong Kong Heritage Museum, the Ten Thousand Buddhas Monastery, and the scenic Shing Mun River.

spots.name: 香港文化博物館 Hong Kong Heritage Museum
spots.description: The largest museum in Hong Kong, covering the territory's history, art, and culture through 12 exhibition galleries. Permanent exhibits include the New Territories Heritage Hall, Cantonese Opera Heritage Hall, and the T.T. Tsui Gallery of Chinese Art. The Bruce Lee exhibition is world-class. The building itself is an architectural landmark.
spots.location: 1 Man Lam Road, Sha Tin
spots.tips: Free admission on Wednesdays. Allow 2-3 hours. The Bruce Lee gallery is a must-see. The museum is a 10-min walk from Sha Tin MTR station.

spots.name: 萬佛寺 Ten Thousand Buddhas Monastery
spots.description: Not actually a monastery but a stunning temple complex with over 12,800 Buddha statues — more than the name suggests. The approach is a steep path lined with larger-than-life golden Buddhist arhat statues (the '500 Arhats'). The main hall houses 1,300 Buddha statues in niches. The views of Sha Tin from the top are excellent.
spots.location: Pai Tau Village, Sha Tin
spots.tips: Free entry. The 400-step climb is steep but rewarding. The arhat statues along the path are fantastic photo subjects. Open 9am-5pm. Combine with a visit to the Heritage Museum.

spots.name: 城門河 Shing Mun River
spots.description: A 7km river running through the heart of Sha Tin, lined with cycling paths, jogging trails, gardens, and parks. Rent a bicycle and ride from Sha Tin to Tai Po along the river — a flat, scenic 12km route. The river is also used for dragon boat racing and rowing.
spots.location: Sha Tin, along the Shing Mun River
spots.tips: Bike rental shops are near Sha Tin MTR station (exits near the river). The ride to Tai Po Waterfront Park is flat and family-friendly. Best in late afternoon for the golden light.

spots.name: 車公廟 Che Kung Temple
spots.description: A large Taoist temple dedicated to Che Kung, a Song dynasty general turned deity. Visitors spin a giant brass windmill to bring good luck — three rotations for maximum fortune. Particularly busy during Chinese New Year when worshippers flock here to pray for good luck in the coming year.
spots.location: Che Kung Temple Road, Tai Wai, Sha Tin
spots.tips: Free entry. The windmill spinning is the main attraction — watch how others do it first. Chinese New Year visits can have 1+ hour queues.

areas.name: 大埔 Tai Po
areas.description: A historic market town turned new town, with a beautiful waterfront park, traditional villages, and the famous Lam Tsuen Wishing Trees.

spots.name: 大埔海濱公園 Tai Po Waterfront Park
spots.description: A massive 22-hectare waterfront park featuring a 32m-high Lookout Tower (the 'Spiral Tower') with panoramic views of Tolo Harbour, a rose garden, insect house, model boat pool, and cycling paths. The park is a favourite for picnics, kite flying, and sunset watching.
spots.location: 1 Wan Tau Kok Lane, Tai Po
spots.tips: Free entry. Climb the Lookout Tower for amazing views. The park connects to the Tai Po cycling path network. Great for a family afternoon out.

spots.name: 林村許願樹 Lam Tsuen Wishing Trees
spots.description: A tradition dating back over 200 years — visitors write wishes on paper scrolls, tie them to oranges, and throw them onto a banyan tree. The higher the throw, the more likely the wish comes true. The original tree is now protected, but a replica tree continues the tradition. Adjacent is the Lam Tsuen open-air museum with traditional Hakka houses.
spots.location: Lam Tsuen, Tai Po
spots.tips: Bus 64K from Tai Po Market MTR. The wishing oranges cost ~HK$25. Most popular during Chinese New Year. The nearby Lam Tsuen Village has a great traditional food market.

spots.name: 香港鐵路博物館 Hong Kong Railway Museum
spots.description: Housed in the former Tai Po Market Railway Station (1913), this free museum showcases the history of Hong Kong's railways. Features the original station building, a narrow-gauge steam locomotive, vintage carriages (including a 1911 first-class carriage with wooden seats), and the Kowloon-Canton Railway history exhibits.
spots.location: 13 Shung Tak Street, Tai Po
spots.tips: Free entry. Climb inside the old train carriages for a nostalgic experience. The colonial station building is photogenic. Allow 45 minutes.

spots.name: 大埔舊墟 Tai Po Old Market
spots.description: The original market of Tai Po, established over 300 years ago. Today the area retains a traditional Chinese market atmosphere with stalls selling everything from fresh produce to household goods. The adjacent Tai Po Hui Market is one of the best wet markets in the New Territories.
spots.location: Tai Po Old Market, near Tai Po Market MTR
spots.tips: Go early morning for the full market experience. The cooked food centre upstairs has excellent, cheap local dishes. The nearby Fuk Man Temple is a hidden gem.

areas.name: 元朗及天水圍 Yuen Long & Tin Shui Wai
areas.description: The northwestern New Territories — a region of traditional walled villages, wetlands, and the historic Ping Shan Heritage Trail.

spots.name: 屏山文物徑 Ping Shan Heritage Trail
spots.description: A 1.6km heritage trail through the historic Tang clan's settlements — one of Hong Kong's oldest and best-preserved traditional walled village areas. Features the 900-year-old Tsui Sing Lau Pagoda (the only surviving ancient pagoda in Hong Kong), the Yu Kiu Ancestral Hall (a magnificent three-hall building), and the Shrine of the Earth God. A declared monument at every stop.
spots.location: Ping Shan, Yuen Long (near Tin Shui Wai MTR)
spots.tips: Free guided tours available on weekends. The Tsui Sing Lau Pagoda is the iconic photo spot. Allow 1.5-2 hours for the full trail.

spots.name: 香港濕地公園 Hong Kong Wetland Park
spots.description: A 61-hectare ecological reserve protecting the Mai Po wetlands ecosystem. Features a large visitor centre, observation hides, boardwalks through marshes and mangroves, and a 'Pui Pui' the crocodile exhibit (a famous crocodile captured in the area). Home to over 200 bird species, mudskippers, fiddler crabs, and otters.
spots.location: Tin Shui Wai, Yuen Long
spots.tips: Take the light rail to Tin Shui Wai. Best visited in winter (Nov-Mar) for migratory bird viewing. The walkway canopy offers close-up views of wetland wildlife. Allow 2-3 hours.

spots.name: 米埔自然保護區 Mai Po Nature Reserve
spots.description: A world-famous wetland reserve — one of the most important bird-watching sites in East Asia. Part of the Ramsar Convention on Wetlands of International Importance. Over 380 bird species have been recorded here, including the endangered Black-faced Spoonbill. The reserve features mangroves, gei wai (shrimp ponds), and boardwalks.
spots.location: Mai Po, Yuen Long
spots.tips: Advance booking required through WWF Hong Kong. Guided tours only (about HK$180). Best birding season is October-April. Binoculars are essential.

spots.name: 元朗錦田吉慶圍 Kat Hing Wai Walled Village (Kam Tin)
spots.description: A well-preserved walled village built by the Tang clan over 500 years ago. Surrounded by a moat and grey-brick walls with cannons at the corners. The village has survived pirate attacks, clan wars, and even the 1899 British takeover (the villagers briefly resisted). The entrance gate is the most photographed spot.
spots.location: Kam Tin, Yuen Long
spots.tips: Free entry. The village is still inhabited — be respectful. The small museum inside has artifacts from the village's history. Combine with a visit to the nearby Yuen Long Old Market.

spots.name: 元朗大馬路 Yuen Long Main Road (Castle Peak Road)
spots.description: The bustling heart of Yuen Long town — a vibrant stretch of Castle Peak Road lined with shops, restaurants, and street food stalls. Famous for the Yuen Long dim sum houses (particularly at the Yuen Long Market), traditional bakeries selling老婆餅 (wife cakes), and the atmospheric old market area.
spots.location: Castle Peak Road, Yuen Long
spots.tips: Try the egg tarts and wife cakes from local bakeries. The Yuen Long Market cooked food centre has excellent, cheap food. Evening is the best time for the street food scene.

areas.name: 北區 North District
areas.description: Hong Kong's northern frontier — a region of historic villages, walled clans, green hiking trails, and the border with mainland China.

spots.name: 龍躍頭文物徑 Lung Yeuk Tau Heritage Trail
spots.description: A heritage trail through the ancient settlements of the Tang clan (one of Hong Kong's 'Five Great Clans'). Features over 30 historic structures including the magnificent Tang Chung Ling Ancestral Hall (built 1525, the largest ancestral hall in Hong Kong), the Lo Wai walled village, the Shek Lo watchtower, and the Shrine of the Earth God.
spots.location: Lung Yeuk Tau, Fanling, North District
spots.tips: Free to walk. The Tang Chung Ling ancestral hall is a declared monument and the highlight. Allow 1.5-2 hours. Start from Fanling MTR station and walk 15min.

spots.name: 粉嶺圍 Fanling Wai
spots.description: Another historic Tang clan walled village (built in the 17th century), surrounded by a moat and defensive walls. The village layout follows strict feng shui principles — a main gate flanked by two cannons, a central ancestral hall, and neatly arranged rows of village houses. Still inhabited by Tang descendants.
spots.location: Fanling, North District (near Fanling MTR)
spots.tips: Free to walk through the public areas. The Tin Hau Temple inside the village is worth a look. Nearby Fanling market has excellent street food.

spots.name: 上水圍 Sheung Shui Wai
spots.description: The ancestral home of the Liu clan — a well-preserved walled village with a history spanning 600 years. The Liu Man Shek Tong Ancestral Hall (1751) is a magnificent three-hall structure with intricate wood carvings and murals. The village retains its original moat, watchtowers, and cannon emplacements.
spots.location: Sheung Shui, North District
spots.tips: Free entry to the ancestral hall. The village is still very much alive — be respectful of residents. Combine with a visit to Sheung Shui Market.

spots.name: 嘉道理農場暨植物園 Kadoorie Farm & Botanic Garden
spots.description: A 148-hectare conservation and education centre in the foothills of Tai Mo Shan. Features breathtaking terraced gardens, a Native Tree Nursery, an orchid house, a butterfly garden, and wildlife rescue centre. The 'Walk with Nature' trails range from 1-hour strolls to full-day hikes. The views of the New Territories from the upper slopes are spectacular.
spots.location: Lam Kam Road, Tai Po (near Fanling border)
spots.tips: Book online in advance (limited daily visitors). The shuttle bus to the top is worth taking for views. The farm cafe serves excellent organic food. Allow 3-4 hours.

spots.name: 鳳園蝴蝶保育區 Fung Yuen Butterfly Reserve
spots.description: One of the most important butterfly habitats in Hong Kong — over 200 butterfly species (about 80% of HK's total) have been recorded in this 42-hectare valley. The reserve features a visitor centre with educational exhibits and guided walks. Peak butterfly season is April-September when the valley comes alive with colour.
spots.location: Fung Yuen, Tai Po (near Ting Kok Road)
spots.tips: Best visited April-September for peak butterfly activity. Guided tours available on weekends. Bring macro photography gear. Entry is free but donations welcome.

areas.name: 荃灣及屯門 Tsuen Wan & Tuen Mun
areas.description: Western New Territories — historic villages, coastal walks, and the starting points for hikes up Tai Mo Shan and Castle Peak.

spots.name: 三棟屋博物館 Sam Tung Uk Museum
spots.description: A beautifully preserved 200-year-old Hakka walled village turned museum. The 'three-beam-roof' village (founded 1786 by the Chan clan) features period furniture, farming tools, and exhibits on Hakka culture. The symmetrical layout with a central ancestral hall is a masterpiece of traditional Chinese village design.
spots.location: 2 Kwu Uk Lane, Tsuen Wan
spots.tips: Free entry. The museum is a 5-min walk from Tsuen Wan MTR station. Allow 45 minutes. The adjacent Tsuen Wan Park is nice for a stroll.

spots.name: 大帽山 Tai Mo Shan
spots.description: Hong Kong's highest peak (957m). The summit is often shrouded in mist, giving it an otherworldly atmosphere. The road to the top is paved (closed to vehicles beyond the BBQ site), making it a popular cycling and running route. On clear days, the panoramic views stretch across the entire territory and into mainland China.
spots.location: Tai Mo Shan Country Park, Tsuen Wan
spots.tips: The road is steep but paved — 7km from the base to the top (2h hike). Bring warm clothes — the summit can be 10°C cooler than the city. Best on clear winter days.

spots.name: 青山禪院及青山灣 Castle Peak Monastery & Castle Peak Beach
spots.description: A historic Buddhist monastery (built 428 AD — one of the oldest in Hong Kong) on the slopes of Castle Peak (583m). The monastery features ornate halls, pagodas, and sweeping views of the Pearl River Delta. Below, Castle Peak Beach is a long, clean beach with excellent swimming and a promenade lined with seafood restaurants.
spots.location: Tsing Shan Monastery Road, Tuen Mun
spots.tips: The monastery is free to enter. The hike to the Castle Peak summit starts from the monastery and takes about 1 hour. The beach is accessible by light rail.

spots.name: 青山灣 Tuen Mun Promenade & Golden Beach
spots.description: A long coastal promenade on the Tuen Mun waterfront, connecting to Golden Beach — one of the finest artificial beaches in Hong Kong with golden sand imported from Hainan. The promenade features the 'Romantic Walk' with sculptures, a beautiful sunset view, and the Ting Kau Bridge in the distance.
spots.location: Tuen Mun, New Territories
spots.tips: The promenade is beautiful at sunset. Golden Beach has good facilities and is less crowded than HK Island beaches. The nearby Tuen Mun Town Plaza is a huge shopping mall.

areas.name: 更多郊野公園及行山 More Country Parks & Hikes
areas.description: Hong Kong is 40% country park — explore more of the green side beyond the city.

spots.name: 麥理浩徑第二段 MacLehose Trail Stage 2
spots.description: Arguably Hong Kong's most scenic day hike — 13.5km from Pak Tam Chung to Ham Tin crossing pristine beaches (Sai Wan, Ham Tin Wan), dramatic headlands, and the iconic hilltop view of the High Island Reservoir. The trail passes through the Sai Kung East Country Park and ends at the remote Tai Long Wan beaches.
spots.location: Pak Tam Chung to Ham Tin, Sai Kung
spots.tips: Start early (7-8am) to finish before noon. 4-5 hours, moderate difficulty. Bring 2L water. Take a speedboat back from Ham Tin to Sai Kung (~HK$150).

spots.name: 清水灣大坳門 Clear Water Bay (Tai O Mun)
spots.description: The eastern tip of Clear Water Bay peninsula — a grassy hillside with spectacular panoramic views of the South China Sea and the distant Ninepin Islands. Popular for kite flying, picnics, and sunset watching. The access road is lined with barbecue pits and food stalls.
spots.location: Tai O Mun Road, Clear Water Bay
spots.tips: Bus 91 from Diamond Hill MTR. Best in late afternoon for sunset. The kite flying here is legendary. The nearby restaurant serves decent squid and noodles.

spots.name: 龍脊 Dragon's Back
spots.description: Named one of the best urban hikes in the world by Time Magazine. The 8.5km ridge walk on the Shek O Peak ridge offers 360-degree views of the South China Sea, Shek O beach, Stanley, and the outlying islands. The trail is easy to moderate and ends at Big Wave Bay where you can cool off in the sea.
spots.location: To Tei Wan to Big Wave Bay, Shek O
spots.tips: Take bus 9 from Shau Kei Wan to To Tei Wan. The trail takes 2-3 hours. Bring a camera — the views are spectacular. End at Big Wave Bay for a swim and a beer at the beach bar.

spots.name: 船灣淡水湖 Plover Cove Reservoir
spots.description: One of Hong Kong's largest reservoirs, formed by damming a sea inlet. The 15km Plover Cove Country Park trail circles the reservoir with stunning views of the Tolo Harbour and the Pat Sin Leng mountain range. The Bride's Pool Waterfall nearby is a popular photo spot.
spots.location: Tai Mei Tuk, Tai Po
spots.tips: Start at Tai Mei Tuk — there's a bike rental if you prefer cycling. The 15km loop takes 4-5 hours on foot. Visit Bride's Pool after heavy rain for the best waterfall views.

spots.name: 八仙嶺 Pat Sin Leng
spots.description: A ridge of eight peaks named after the Eight Immortals of Chinese mythology. The 12km hike from Tai Mei Tuk to Sha Tau Kok offers unparalleled views of Plover Cove, Tolo Harbour, and across the border into mainland China. Each peak is named after a different immortal.
spots.location: Tai Mei Tuk to Sha Tau Kok, Tai Po
spots.tips: A challenging 5-6 hour hike with steep ascents. Best in cooler months (Nov-Feb). Bring 3L water minimum. The descent to Sha Tau Kok has stunning coastal views.

spots.name: 大欖涌水塘 Tai Lam Chung Reservoir
spots.description: Often called the 'Thousand Island Lake' of Hong Kong — a serpentine reservoir with multiple coves and inlets surrounded by lush green hills. The 10km trail around it offers peaceful hiking far from the crowds. The reservoir features a scenic dam and picnic areas.
spots.location: Tai Lam Chung, Tuen Mun
spots.tips: Start from the Tai Lam Chung BBQ site. The trail is mostly flat and takes 3 hours. Great for cycling too. The views from the dam are spectacular at sunset.

spots.name: 青山腹地 Castle Peak Hinterland
spots.description: A wild, lunar-like landscape of eroded granite badlands — one of Hong Kong's least-visited hiking areas. The terrain is rugged with no shade, making it feel like another planet. Features the abandoned 'No Name' village and the mysterious 'pyramid hill'.
spots.location: Castle Peak, Tuen Mun
spots.tips: Extremely difficult — no shade, no water sources, and poorly marked trails. Only attempt in cool weather with a GPS. Bring 4L water. The landscape is surreal but dangerous in summer.

areas.name: 更多沙灘 More Beaches
areas.description: Hidden and less-crowded beaches across the New Territories and outlying islands.

spots.name: 三星灣 Trio Beach
spots.description: A small, sheltered beach in Clear Water Bay with crystal-clear waters and fine golden sand. Accessible only by a 20-minute walk from the road or by kaito from Sai Kung. The water quality is consistently rated 'excellent' — among the cleanest in Hong Kong. Popular with snorkelers.
spots.location: Trio Beach, Clear Water Bay
spots.tips: Walk 20 min from Tai Au Mun road or take a kaito from Sai Kung pier. The beach is small and fills up on weekends. Go early. The snorkeling is great on the rocky edges.

spots.name: 洪聖爺灣 Hung Shing Yeh Beach
spots.description: The most popular beach on Lamma Island — a clean, family-friendly stretch of sand with a famous waterfront restaurant (Tung Kee) serving excellent seafood. The waters are calm and safe for swimming. Backed by the Lamma Power Station's distinctive chimneys.
spots.location: Yung Shue Wan, Lamma Island
spots.tips: 20-min walk from Yung Shue Wan ferry. The seafood at Tung Kee is legendary. Combine with a hike to Sok Kwu Wan. Gets crowded on weekends.

spots.name: 大嶺及東灣山 Tai Leng Tung & Tung Wan (Cheung Chau)
spots.description: Cheung Chau's highest point (94m) offering a stunning 360-degree view of the island's distinctive dumbbell shape. The short hike takes 15-20 minutes from the harbour. The adjacent Tung Wan Beach is Cheung Chau's main swimming beach with soft sand and calm waters.
spots.location: Cheung Chau Island
spots.tips: The Tai Leng Tung hike starts from the Cheung Chau Sports Ground. Sunset from the top is spectacular. Tung Wan Beach has great cafes and the Warwick Hotel right on the sand.

spots.name: 草灣 Tso Wan (Grass Bay)
spots.description: A hidden, unspoiled beach on the remote northwestern coast of Lantau — no facilities, no crowds, just pristine sand and turquoise water. Accessible only by boat or a difficult hike. The beach is backed by abandoned farmhouses and bamboo groves.
spots.location: Tso Wan, Lantau Island
spots.tips: Accessible by private boat or via the 3-hour hike from Tung Chung. Bring ALL supplies — no shops, no fresh water. This is for experienced hikers only. The isolation is the point.

spots.name: 銀礦灣 Silver Mine Bay Beach
spots.description: Mui Wo's main beach — a long, sandy crescent lined with pine trees and backed by the village. The water is calm and shallow, perfect for families. Named after the now-abandoned silver mines in the nearby hills. The sunset views over the distant Chi Ma Wan peninsula are beautiful.
spots.location: Mui Wo, Lantau Island
spots.tips: A 10-min walk from Mui Wo ferry. The beach is long enough that you can always find a quiet spot. The Silvermine Cave (abandoned mine) is a 20-min walk uphill.

areas.name: 更多離島 More Outlying Islands
areas.description: The wilder, lesser-visited islands of Hong Kong — from volcanic sea arches to uninhabited wilderness.

spots.name: 甕缸群島 Ninepin Group
spots.description: A spectacular group of volcanic islands in the Hong Kong UNESCO Global Geopark, famous for towering sea cliffs, sea arches, and the 'Devil's Fist' rock formation. The hexagonal volcanic columns here are among the finest in the world. Accessible only by chartered boat.
spots.location: Sai Kung waters (offshore)
