spots.tips: Charter a boat from Sai Kung for the day (~HK$3000-4000 for a group). The seas can be rough — check weather conditions. Best photographed from a boat at sunset. Don't attempt to land without a guide.

spots.name: 果洲群島 Ninepin Group (Kwo Chau Islands)
spots.description: Two main islands (North Ninepin and South Ninepin) and 27 smaller islets forming the most dramatic volcanic seascape in Hong Kong. Towering sea stacks, blowholes, and the iconic 'Eyeball Rock' — a round sea arch that looks like an eye. A paradise for photographers and kayakers.
spots.location: Off Sai Kung Peninsula
spots.tips: Only accessible by private boat or guided kayak tour. No facilities whatsoever. The water is crystal clear — excellent for snorkeling when calm. Spring and autumn are the best seasons.

spots.name: 馬灣 Ma Wan
spots.description: A small island between Lantau and Tsing Yi, now connected by bridge. Features the Ma Wan Park (with a stunning Noah's Ark theme park), the Tung Wan Beach with a view of the Tsing Ma Bridge, and a relocated fishing village. The sunset view of the bridge from the beach is iconic.
spots.location: Ma Wan, between Lantau and Tsing Yi
spots.tips: Bus NR330 from Tsing Yi MTR or ferry from Central. The Noah's Ark park is child-friendly. The beach has the best view of the Tsing Ma Bridge — great for photos.

areas.name: 更多偏遠離島 More Remote Islands
areas.description: Hong Kong has over 260 islands — these are the wildest, most remote, and least-visited. Most Hongkongers have never set foot on any of them.

spots.name: 橫瀾島 Waglan Island
spots.description: A remote island at the southeastern entrance to Hong Kong's waters, home to the 1893 Waglan Lighthouse — one of the most beautifully preserved lighthouses in Asia. The lighthouse is still operational and automated. The island has a weather station and stunning 360-degree ocean views. Access is strictly controlled but occasional guided tours are organized by the Marine Department.
spots.location: Southeastern waters of Hong Kong (about 5km east of Po Toi)
spots.tips: Not open to the public except on special open days organized by the Marine Department (~once a year). The lighthouse is a declared monument. Best viewed from a boat tour passing by.

spots.name: 青洲 Green Island
spots.description: A small island off the coast of Kennedy Town, home to the 1875 Green Island Lighthouse (the oldest surviving lighthouse in Hong Kong). The island features abandoned lightkeepers' quarters, a helipad, and stunning views back at the HK Island skyline. The waters around it are popular with divers. No public ferry — only accessible by private boat.
spots.location: Off Kennedy Town, Western District (10-min boat ride)
spots.tips: No public access to the island itself (restricted area). However, the view from Kennedy Town promenade is excellent. Boat tours that circle the island are available. The lighthouse is best photographed from the water.

spots.name: 喜靈洲 Hei Ling Chau
spots.description: An island with a dark past — site of a former leper colony (1910s-1970s) and now a drug rehabilitation centre. The abandoned buildings, overgrown pathways, and empty churches create an eerie, atmospheric landscape frozen in time. The old leper colony chapel is hauntingly beautiful. The island also has a lighthouse and a small beach. There's a regular ferry but visitors need a permit.
spots.location: Off Lantau Island (ferry from Central Pier 4, then change at Peng Chau)
spots.tips: The island is restricted — you need a permit from the Correctional Services Department to visit. The ferry runs but only for staff/visitors. For most people, viewing from a boat tour is the only option. The abandoned chapel is the most photographed spot.

spots.name: 索罟群島 Soko Islands
spots.description: A remote group of islands (Tai A Chau, Si A Chau, Lo Chau) in the far southwestern waters, closer to Macau than Hong Kong Island. Wild, uninhabited, and pristine — no facilities, no roads, no people. The beaches are untouched with crystal-clear water. Sea turtles have been spotted nesting here. Only accessible by private junk or kayak expedition.
spots.location: Southwestern waters of Hong Kong (~20km from Cheung Chau)
spots.tips: No ferry service. Charter a boat from Cheung Chau or Aberdeen. Bring ALL supplies — there's NOTHING on the islands. The snorkeling is spectacular. Best visited as a multi-day kayak camping trip for experienced paddlers.

spots.name: 鴨洲 Ap Chau (Duck Island)
spots.description: A tiny island in the far northeast of Hong Kong's waters, shaped like a duck (hence the name). The island has a small Hakka fishing village with a single row of houses, a Tin Hau Temple, and a unique geological formation — a sea arch called the 'Duck's Eye'. The island is connected to the mainland of China by the Sha Tau Kok border. Very few visitors make it here.
spots.location: Sha Tau Kok waters, northeastern Hong Kong
spots.tips: Requires a permit for the Sha Tau Kok border area (now open for group tours). Alternatively, join a guided geopark boat tour. The 'Duck's Eye' sea arch is the highlight. Combine with a visit to Kat O and the northeast geopark.

spots.name: 往灣洲 Round Island (Wong Wan Chau)
spots.description: Part of the Hong Kong UNESCO Global Geopark, this uninhabited island in the northeast features striking sedimentary rock formations, sea arches, and a spectacular shoreline of red sandstone. The island is covered in dense woodland and has no human habitation. The 'Round Island' name comes from its distinctive rounded shape when viewed from the sea.
spots.location: Northeastern waters, part of the Geopark
spots.tips: Accessible by chartered boat from Ma Liu Shui pier. Part of the northeast geopark boat tour route. The red sandstone cliffs are most dramatic in late afternoon light. No facilities — bring water and food.

spots.name: 螺洲 Beaufort Island (Lo Chau)
spots.description: A small, uninhabited island south of Hong Kong Island with a distinctive conical shape. The island is entirely wild — no buildings, no trails, no people. The waters around it are crystal clear and popular with sea kayakers. The island has a small pebble beach on its northern side where kayakers sometimes land. It's visible from Stanley and Po Toi.
spots.location: South of Stanley / north of Po Toi
spots.tips: Only accessible by kayak or private boat. No landing facilities — you'll need to haul your kayak up the pebble beach. The water clarity is excellent for snorkeling. Do NOT attempt in rough seas.

spots.name: 宋崗 Sung Kong
spots.description: A remote island south of Hong Kong Island, home to an automated lighthouse and a former British military radio station. The island is rugged and windswept with spectacular sea cliffs. The lighthouse, built in 1950s, marks the southeastern approach to Hong Kong's waters. The island is completely uninhabited and off-limits to landing.
spots.location: Southern waters, east of Lamma Island
spots.tips: No public landing allowed. Best viewed on a boat tour from Aberdeen. The waters around Sung Kong are excellent for fishing. Pair with a trip past Po Toi and Beaufort Island.

spots.name: 火石洲 Fu Tau Fan Chau (Basalt Island)
spots.description: Part of the UNESCO Global Geopark, this uninhabited island in the Sai Kung waters is famous for its stunning hexagonal volcanic columns and towering sea cliffs. The island forms one side of the dramatic 'Basalt Island' strait, where the water channel creates powerful currents. The geological formations here are world-class.
spots.location: Sai Kung waters, part of the Geopark
spots.tips: Accessible by chartered boat from Sai Kung. Combines well with a tour of the Ninepin Group and High Island. The hexagonal columns are most impressive up close from the water. Do not attempt to land — the currents are dangerous.

spots.name: 鴨脷洲 Ap Lei Chau
spots.description: Technically Hong Kong's third-largest island and the most densely populated island in the world (by some measures). Connected to Hong Kong Island by the Ap Lei Chau Bridge. Features the Aberdeen Marina, a large shopping mall (South Horizons Plaza), and a waterfront promenade with stunning views back at the Aberdeen Typhoon Shelter and HK Island. Most visitors don't even realize it's an island.
spots.location: Adjacent to Aberdeen, Southern District
spots.tips: Take bus 90 or 99 from Central. The waterfront promenade at South Horizons has the best sunset view of Aberdeen. The fishing port at the old Ap Lei Chau area is worth exploring.
